name: pair_device
description: Add/pair or remove a physical device -- callable any time, including mid-Plan-session. Ask the customer what protocol (insteon, z-wave, zigbee, matter, x10) if unclear. insteon/zwave/zigbee/matter are wired up; x10 returns a not-yet-supported message -- walk the customer through manual pairing instead. A Z-Wave controller still running the Legacy (pre-Z-Matter) generation returns a clear error for any zwave action -- tell the customer to use the ISY administrative console for that controller. IMPORTANT for adding a zwave/zigbee/matter device: there is no such thing as a customer-readable device address for these protocols, and add_by_address is not a valid action for them at all (see _PROTOCOL_ACTIONS). Once the customer says they want to add a device of one of these protocols, protocol is the only thing this call needs -- call include immediately, in this same turn, with no clarifying question of any kind first. This means: never ask whether they know the device's address (not even rhetorically, e.g. 'you probably don't have an address, right?'); never present 'address vs. pairing mode' as a choice; and never ask for device_type either -- it's optional, so just omit it unless the customer already volunteered it unprompted. Do not make the customer confirm anything before you open pairing mode -- open it, then tell them what to do. Asking any question here before calling include is exactly the fabrication/stalling pattern to avoid: there is nothing to clarify. CRITICAL -- include/exclude BLOCK for up to ~80s waiting for the customer's own physical action, and they do it on their own screen, not in this chat: before calling either action, say your instructions to the customer as your own plain text in this same reply, immediately before the tool call (e.g. 'I've put the hub in pairing mode -- follow the instructions on your screen to add the device.') -- never 'let me know when you're done' or any variant expecting a chat reply, because there won't be one; the customer interacts with an on-screen dialog that eisy-ui shows them directly, and this call already waits for that to finish on its own. Getting the wording right matters: say the instructions BEFORE making the call in the same response (that text reaches the customer immediately, while the call is still running), never after -- text written after the tool call in your reply is what you say once it's already done. Action depends on protocol: add_by_address (insteon/x10 only -- these are the only protocols with a customer-readable address in this system) is for a device whose own address the customer already knows or can read off the unit -- this call itself waits (up to ~80s) for the new device to actually become usable before returning, so it's safe to reference the returned device_address in the very next tool call. include (insteon/zwave/zigbee) opens pairing mode and waits for that protocol's own pairing session to end (however long the customer takes, up to ~80s), then returns whatever was newly discovered directly in its own result's new_devices list (address + whatever name the hub assigned, usually blank -- no separate lookup needed to find or name them; rename via node_op using that address). insteon's pairing window supports multiple devices in one call -- the customer can activate several before finishing on their screen, and all of them come back in new_devices. include for matter is NOT implemented via chat -- adding a Matter device needs a pairing code/QR code this tool has no way to accept, so calling it just returns a message telling the customer to use the eisy-ui interface directly; don't bother calling it expecting it to actually pair a Matter device. exclude (zwave/zigbee/matter only -- insteon has no distinct hardware remove mode here) removes a device, but whether device_address is required depends on the protocol -- this is the one place add/remove aren't symmetric, so don't assume: for zwave, device_address is OPTIONAL and should normally be omitted -- the customer identifies the device physically (pressing its own exclude button once the hub is listening), not by name in chat, so there is nothing to ask them to confirm or disambiguate; just open removal mode and tell them to activate the device, the hub reports back which one it was. Only pass device_address for zwave if the customer already volunteered a specific address unprompted. For zigbee/matter, device_address IS required (resolve it from DEVICE DATABASE first, never guess) -- there is no physical activation window for these, the call removes that exact address directly. Behavior differs by protocol group, and this matters for how you talk to the customer: for zwave, this opens removal mode and waits (same ~80s budget) for the customer to activate the device on their own, then reports whichever device the hub excluded in removed_devices -- same 'say instructions before calling' rule as include, and never ask 'which device' first. For zigbee/matter, there is no window or on-screen step at all -- the call performs the ENTIRE removal immediately and returns status=exclusion_committed with removed_devices already populated; do not tell the customer to do anything on-screen for these two, and do not call this twice -- one call is the whole operation, done. Zigbee specifically can fail silently at the network layer: instead of actually removing the node, the hub sometimes just disables it locally, and this call detects that and returns an error (with device_address) instead of a false 'success' -- if you get that error, tell the customer the device could not be removed from the Zigbee network and they need to remove it manually from the eisy-ui interface, linking it as /nodes/{device_address} per UI NAVIGATION RULES. For adding a marketplace plugin (not a physical device), use install_plugin/buy_plugin instead -- that's a different kind of entity with its own link space (/plugins/...). A physical device this tool adds/pairs/removes, regardless of protocol, is a device node: when you mention it in your reply, link it as /nodes/{address} per UI NAVIGATION RULES (using the address this tool's own result just gave you, e.g. new_devices[].address) -- never a /plugins/... link, that's only ever for the plugin marketplace/dashboard/licenses, not for a device a plugin happens to have created either. When the customer names a specific device to remove, never guess its protocol from the device's name/model to pick this call's protocol argument -- that's a fabrication risk identical to stating the protocol out loud. Either call get_device_family (via get_diagnostics_prompt/run_diagnostic_step) first, or just try node_op(delete, node_id=...): it succeeds directly for insteon, and for zwave/zigbee/matter/plugin it's rejected with the device's real protocol/flow named in the error, so you never have to guess which protocol to pass here.

action.description: add_by_address is insteon/x10 ONLY (needs device_address) -- not a valid action for zwave/zigbee/matter, which have no customer-readable address before pairing; use include for those instead, never ask the customer for an address. include (add) works for insteon/zwave/zigbee -- opens pairing mode and blocks until the customer completes it on their own screen (or times out), then returns new_devices directly; for matter it instead returns a message directing the customer to the eisy-ui interface, since chat-based Matter pairing isn't implemented. exclude (remove) works for zwave/zigbee/matter only -- for zwave, device_address is OPTIONAL (the customer identifies the device physically, not by name -- just open removal mode and blocks the same way as include); for zigbee/matter, device_address IS required and it performs the whole removal in this one call, immediately, no window.

device_address.description: The device's own physical address, exactly as shown in DEVICE DATABASE. Required for action=add_by_address, and for action=exclude when protocol is zigbee/matter (a specific address is removed directly). NOT required for action=exclude when protocol is zwave -- omit it there; the customer identifies the device physically and the hub reports back which one was excluded.

device_type.description: Optional device-type hint (add_by_address/include). Never ask the customer for this before calling -- omit it unless they already mentioned the device type unprompted; it is not worth delaying the call for.
